Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Our SOC 2 Type II (2026 period) covers Redwood's hosted API and the Redwood control plane that we operate (multi-tenant hosted offering). It does not automatically include customer-managed Dedicated pools that you provision in your own VPC or on-prem install.

2) For Dedicated / VPC / on-prem customers we offer two artifacts: (a) a standard bridge letter that maps Redwood-managed controls to the Dedicated/VPC operating model and (b) evidence packages for common control points where Redwood still provides a managed service (e.g., key rotation APIs, logging ingest). The bridge letter is not a separate SOC 2 report but is intended to help auditors understand applicability.

3) Latest report covers 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31 — I'll attach the PDF and a bridge-letter template.

I'll loop in Marissa from Compliance and Karthik from Solutions to confirm the exact evidence we can provide for VPC deployments (logs, audit hooks, encryption key flow diagrams). If you can share the specific controls you care about (CC6, CC7, etc.) or your SIG/CAIQ matrix rows, we can prioritize.

Next steps: I'll drop the SOC 2 PDF and a bridge letter template now; Marissa will follow up with evidence availability and timelines.

Hi Elena — Marissa from Compliance here. Adding more color on the Dedicated/VPC split and what we can furnish:

- Scope: The formal SOC 2 report scope is Redwood's control environment for the hosted control plane and the managed hosted inference endpoints. Dedicated pools that run in customer VPCs under a reserved contract are considered "customer-hosted/isolated" for the purposes of SOC scoping unless the customer opts into Redwood-managed networking and logging where we retain certain control responsibilities.

- Bridge letters: We maintain a bridge letter template that explains which trust service criteria are the responsibility of Redwood vs customer for Dedicated/VPC/on-prem patterns. Typical items covered: patching windows for Redwood-managed instances, key management responsibilities, access provisioning to the Redwood control plane, and log retention when using Redwood ingest.

- Evidence: For VPC deployments we can provide: evidence of our control plane's logging and monitoring (retention policies, SIEM ingest samples), encryption-at-rest configuration docs, SOC 2 control mappings, and the SOC 2 PDF. We cannot produce tenant-level system images for customer-managed Dedicated instances.

- Audit period: Confirmed 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. If FintechCo's auditor needs an attestation covering a later period we can discuss an interim bridge letter that references ongoing controls and a timeline for producing a refreshed evidence bundle.

Please tell us which controls your auditor will dig into first (or share a short list from your SIG/CAIQ) and we will prioritize pulling the artifacts. I can also schedule a 30-minute call with our compliance engineer to walk through the mapping.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Compliance & Privacy | Redwood Inference

The full evidence bundle (logs, KMS flow diagram, sample retention policy, and control mappings) we can assemble within 7 business days (by 2027-03-01), assuming no blockers on NDA/access.

2) NDA/Data transfer: We do not require an external NDA to share the SOC 2 PDF. It is designed for auditors to reconcile gaps rather than replace a full SOC 2.
